issues.response: Thank you for reconciling by reading instead of repeating the writes, and for the receipts. We could not establish the root cause and do not claim that every network break is gone: the Windows event log of the DEV server shows no restart of the MCP service between 22:04 UTC on 24 October and 08:43 UTC on 25 October (your session was not lost to a restart), and sandbox_call returns the API's answer, or its own error, as a tool result, never by dropping the connection. 'Transport closed' is what an MCP client reports when the connection, its session or the answer's event stream breaks between it and the server, whatever the tool did. What the server had was the most fragile transport the protocol allows: a stateful session kept in the MCP process's memory (reaped after 30 idle minutes) and every answer sent as an event stream through the TLS gateway, which also compresses it, and your VPN. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) the MCP server is stateless with plain JSON answers: each tool call is one HTTP request and its answer, with no session id to lose and no stream held open (no tool needed either). Your agent needs no change; reconnect it once after the upgrade (a new agent session). (2) sandbox_status returns recent_calls: your implementation's last 20 sandbox_call outcomes, newest first (method, path, as_user, idempotency_key, outcome, status, request_id, idempotent_replay, ms, error_type), kept per developer and implementation in the MCP service's memory (a restart empties it). outcome is answered (with the API's status and request_id), refused or failed (stopped before sending), not_sent (no connection: the API never saw the request), uncertain (sent, and the API's answer never reached the MCP server) or 'no answer recorded' (still running, or the tool call itself was cut off). A key the sandbox generates is recorded before the request is sent, so you see it in every case. (3) When the answer is lost between the MCP server and the API, sandbox_call itself answers outcome uncertain or not_sent with error_type, the elapsed ms and the original idempotency_key, instead of a bare error. Nothing is ever retried. After a transport error, read recent_calls first: answered gives you the lost answer; after uncertain or 'no answer recorded', re-read the record and follow the endpoint's write_semantics, and repeat a write only with the same idempotency_key and payload on an endpoint that takes one, exactly as you did by hand. Frontend guide 10 (the sandbox section and the tool table) says this. If an answer is lost again, report the UTC time, server_build, method and path and the recent_calls entry: it tells us whether the API answered, and we will read the gateway's and the MCP service's logs for that minute.
